description: Baseline: streaming Keylock engine quality benchmark (real music 40s slow/fast/identity/ride + sine ride). quality=81.87

asi.hypothesis: baseline
asi.biggest_levers: transient_f1 fast render 0.489 (smearing on speedup); identity_corr 0.505 at rate 1.0 (keylock chain not transparent)

description: Harness calibration (not a DSP change): compensate reported pipeline latency in transient F1, phase-blind identity metric (LR8 allpass), add hard ±14-16% ratios. New effective baseline 95.34.

asi.hypothesis: harness had latency bias + phase-sensitive identity metric
asi.finding: transient_f1 0.61->0.92 purely from latency compensation; identity xcorr 0.50 was allpass phase, spectral sim is 0.991
asi.levers: spec_sim slow2 (-16%) = 0.916 worst; transient_f1 ~0.92 all rates

description: SOLA TRANSIENT_POSTPONE_RATIO 3.0→1.8: postpone splices near weaker energy bursts. transient_f1 0.9188→0.9210, tiny but real (deterministic bench).

asi.hypothesis: more conservative online transient postpone protects more attacks
asi.result: +0.066 quality via transient_f1 +0.0022; small because postpone only delays, doesn't relocate splices
asi.next: try shorter/longer XFADE, DRIFT_TRIGGER, or outgoing-span energy check

description: DRIFT_TRIGGER 192→128 + HARD 320→256: more frequent smaller splices. Worse everywhere: spec −0.0014, transient −0.0023, pitch p95 0.43→0.71c.

asi.hypothesis: smaller more frequent splices reduce per-splice damage
asi.rollback_reason: quality 95.41→94.76; more splices = more fades = more pitch wobble and more attack smears
asi.next_action_hint: try the opposite: LARGER drift trigger (fewer splices), e.g. 256/384

description: DRIFT_TRIGGER 192→256 + HARD 320→448: fewer larger splices. Also worse: transient_f1 0.921→0.902, pitch 0.43→0.55c. 192/320 is a local optimum.

asi.hypothesis: fewer larger splices = less total fade damage
asi.rollback_reason: quality 95.41→94.63; larger jumps skip/repeat more audio per splice, hurting transients (0.921→0.902)
asi.learning: DRIFT/HARD trigger 192/320 is locally optimal in both directions; stop tuning it
asi.next_action_hint: focus on splice PLACEMENT (online onset detection feeding OnsetEvents) instead of splice frequency

description: Online onset detection at SOLA ingest (RMS jump 2.5x, refractory 46ms) feeding both splice protection and masked-window placement. transient_f1 0.921→0.910 — worse.

asi.hypothesis: online attack detection at ingest (~13ms lookahead) protects transients from splice fades
asi.rollback_reason: quality 95.41→95.07, transient_f1 0.921→0.910
asi.suspect: masked-window opportunistic splices now fire 17-46ms AFTER each detected kick — inside the kick body/decay — smearing it; or postponed splices get forced at HARD_TRIGGER in worse spots
asi.next_action_hint: retry with online onsets used for span PROTECTION only (not masked-window placement)

description: Online onset detection, protection-only variant (no masked-window use). Still worse than baseline: transient_f1 0.921→0.915.

asi.hypothesis: online onsets for fade-span protection only
asi.rollback_reason: quality 95.41→95.22; transient_f1 still down 0.921→0.915
asi.learning: onset protection postpones splices past DRIFT_TRIGGER; the forced splices at HARD_TRIGGER are then LARGER jumps, which experiment #4/#5 showed hurt more than fade-through-transient does. The existing energy-postpone (1.8x) already covers the useful cases
asi.next_action_hint: stop onset-protection direction; attack transient smearing differently — e.g. splice landing refinement, or XFADE shape/length

description: XFADE_FRAMES 96→64 (~1.45ms splice fades): transient_f1 0.921→0.928, quality 95.41→95.58. Pitch max 0.53→0.69c (still tiny vs 22c gate).

asi.hypothesis: shorter fades smear less audio per splice
asi.result: +0.17 quality; transient_f1 +0.007, spec unchanged, pitch max slightly up (0.53→0.69c, harmless)
asi.next: try 48 to find the knee; watch clicks_per_m and pitch

description: XFADE_FRAMES 64→48: too short. transient_f1 0.928→0.913. 64 is the knee.

asi.hypothesis: even shorter fades = even less smear
asi.rollback_reason: quality 95.58→95.13; 48-frame fades cause spectral splatter that reads as onset timing damage
asi.learning: XFADE knee is at 64; keep 64
asi.next_action_hint: different lever: splice correlation window / search shape, or spec_sim at hard ratios

description: TRANSIENT_POSTPONE_RATIO 1.8→1.4: too aggressive, postponed splices get forced bigger. transient_f1 0.928→0.912.

asi.hypothesis: postpone even more splices near bursts
asi.rollback_reason: quality 95.58→95.10; over-postponement forces bigger jumps later (same failure mode as onset protection)
asi.learning: postpone ratio sweet spot is ~1.8; the postpone-vs-forced-jump tradeoff is sharp
asi.next_action_hint: try SEARCH_RANGE or CORR_WINDOW enlargement for better splice landings

description: SEARCH_RANGE 160→224: worse (spec 0.957→0.955, transient 0.928→0.919) and slower (85x→50x). Wider search parks drift further off nominal.

asi.hypothesis: wider search finds better-correlated landings
asi.rollback_reason: quality 95.58→95.27; distant candidates win ties and park drift off-nominal, and cost 40% throughput
asi.learning: SEARCH_RANGE 160 is right; splice params are all near a local optimum. Parameter tuning on SOLA is exhausted
asi.next_action_hint: structural: improve varispeed resampler quality, or attach artifact path as an additional benchmark scenario, or low-band handling at hard ratios

description: Harness sensitivity fix: transient detection hop 512→256 (measured ceiling was F1≈0.93 from quantization; now ≈0.99). New effective baseline 96.13. Real F1 headroom now visible: slow2 0.939 / fast2 0.934.

asi.hypothesis: transient_f1 was at detector-quantization ceiling
asi.finding: hop 512 self-shift F1=0.92-0.94; hop 256 = 0.98-1.0. Previous SOLA tuning partly fit quantization noise (XFADE 64 keep may need re-validation)
asi.levers: transient_f1 at hard ratios (0.934-0.939), spec_sim slow2 0.916 (low band by design)

description: Revert XFADE_FRAMES 64→96: the earlier 64-keep was fitting detector quantization noise. Under fixed metric 96 wins (96.26 vs 96.13), pitch back to 0.43/0.53c.

asi.hypothesis: XFADE 64 keep was noise-fit; re-test under hop-256 metric
asi.finding: 96-frame fades better: transient_f1 0.9463→0.9496 AND pitch 0.45/0.69→0.43/0.53. Lesson: never trust sub-ceiling metric wins
asi.learning: all SOLA params now re-anchored at original values except TRANSIENT_POSTPONE_RATIO=1.8 (kept from #3, small)

description: Re-validate TRANSIENT_POSTPONE_RATIO 3.0 vs kept 1.8: 1.8 confirmed better under fixed metric (96.26 vs 96.06, transient 0.9496 vs 0.9428). Keeping 1.8.

asi.hypothesis: check whether postpone 1.8 keep was also noise-fit
asi.rollback_reason: 3.0 is worse; 1.8 is genuinely better (+0.007 F1)
asi.learning: postpone 1.8 validated under trustworthy metric; SOLA params final: DRIFT 192/320, XFADE 96, SEARCH 160, postpone 1.8

description: Splice distance penalty 0.02→0.05: worse (F1 0.9496→0.9429). Correlation quality matters more than drift centering.

asi.hypothesis: stronger pull toward nominal reduces drift timing skew
asi.rollback_reason: 96.26→96.01; worse-correlated landings hurt more than centered drift helps
asi.next_action_hint: try CORR_WINDOW 448, then move to structural ideas

description: CORR_WINDOW 320→448: F1 up (0.9511) but spec down, pitch p95 0.43→1.46c, and seam-recovery test fails (−6.69 dB parked drift de-phasing). Worse overall anyway.

asi.hypothesis: longer corr window aligns low-mid content better at splices
asi.rollback_reason: seam_level_recovers_after_a_nudge fails (-6.69dB); quality 94.34 anyway (spec/pitch degrade)
asi.learning: CORR_WINDOW interacts with rest-recentering: longer window biases splice landings and parks drift that de-phases the crossover seam. 320 is load-bearing
asi.next_action_hint: SOLA micro-tuning fully exhausted; go structural (low-band at hard ratios, or varispeed resampler)

description: Quiet-gap opportunistic splicing (drift>96 + both spans <0.6x avg energy → splice early): quality 96.26→96.39, transient_f1 0.9496→0.9538, pitch unchanged.

asi.hypothesis: splice early in quiet gaps so fewer splices are forced near attacks
asi.result: +0.13 quality via F1 +0.004; first structural win. Placement > protection confirmed
asi.next: tune QUIET_SPLICE_RATIO (0.5? 0.75?) and/or lower the quiet-splice drift threshold

description: QUIET_SPLICE_RATIO 0.6→0.75: too permissive, splices in medium-energy audio. F1 0.9538→0.9397.

asi.hypothesis: more quiet-gap splices = fewer forced ones
asi.rollback_reason: 96.39→95.96; 0.75x avg is not actually quiet in dense EDM
asi.next_action_hint: try 0.45–0.5 (stricter)

description: QUIET_SPLICE_RATIO 0.6→0.5: also worse (F1 0.9538→0.9409). 0.6 is the sweet spot.

asi.hypothesis: stricter quiet gate
asi.rollback_reason: 96.39→96.00; non-monotone response — 0.5 misses useful gaps AND changes which splices happen (chaotic re-timing)
asi.learning: QUIET_SPLICE_RATIO=0.6 locally optimal; note metric responds chaotically to splice-timing changes (±0.01 F1), treat small deltas skeptically
asi.next_action_hint: lower OPPORTUNISTIC_DRIFT for quiet splicing (e.g. 64) so corrections are even smaller, or move on to identity/spec levers

description: Harness: add 2nd scored track (Hot Stuff, disco-house 120bpm) — overfit guard. New effective baseline 95.06; track B transient_f1 is much worse (0.82-0.91), real headroom found.

asi.hypothesis: single-track score risks overfitting to splice timing
asi.finding: Hot Stuff F1: slow 0.906 fast 0.861 slow2 0.861 fast2 0.819 — far worse than track A; speedups worst. Spec similar between tracks
asi.levers: track B transient_f1 fast2=0.819 is the biggest target now

description: Revert TRANSIENT_POSTPONE_RATIO 1.8→3.0 (original): on the 2-track metric 3.0 is slightly better (95.08 vs 95.06). The 1.8 keep was track-A overfit.

asi.hypothesis: re-validate 1.8 postpone on 2-track metric
asi.finding: 1.8 was track-A overfit; 3.0 marginally better overall and is the original value. Also need to re-validate quiet-gap splicing (kept on 1-track metric)
asi.learning: every single-track-tuned param must be re-checked; deltas <0.1 quality are suspect

description: Ablation: remove quiet-gap splicing → 95.08→94.67, F1 0.9084→0.8948. Confirms quiet-gap placement is a real cross-track win. Restored.

asi.hypothesis: ablate quiet-gap splicing to validate on 2-track metric
asi.finding: quiet-gap is worth +0.41 quality / +0.014 F1 across both tracks — the one validated DSP win so far
asi.next_action_hint: investigate track B specifics: why is fast2 F1 0.819? maybe drift timing skew on sparser material; try lowering quiet-gap drift threshold 96→64

description: Quiet-gap drift threshold 96→64: worse (F1 0.908→0.899). More small splices ≠ better; 96 stands.

asi.hypothesis: correct drift even earlier in quiet gaps
asi.rollback_reason: 95.08→94.79; every extra splice costs, even in quiet audio (sinc-read phase scramble at each fade)
asi.learning: splice count minimization matters as much as placement; drift threshold 96 confirmed
asi.next_action_hint: study track B failure mode directly: dump splice positions vs missed onsets, or check if B's segment has quieter/sparser gaps

description: Skip-span attack protection for forward splices (both variants: postpone-only and forced-cap): identical 94.88, worse than 95.08. Fast-render F1 dropped despite protecting exactly the hypothesized deletion mechanism.

asi.hypothesis: forward splices delete attacks in the skipped span; cap jumps before bursts
asi.rollback_reason: 94.88 vs 95.08; A-slow renders improved but both fast renders worsened
asi.learning: revised failure theory: missing onsets at speedup are regularly spaced (every 2 beats = snare/clap class) — likely NOT individual deletions but the output ODF noise floor rising from dense splice flux (~every 38ms at +13%), drowning the 2nd-loudest onset class in median+MAD thresholding. Protection can't fix that; need fewer/cleaner splices at fast rates
asi.next_action_hint: re-test DRIFT 256/HARD 384 on the 2-track metric (prev test was track-A only); or improve splice correlation quality at small transpositions

description: XFADE 96→128 on 2-track metric: worse (95.03 vs 95.08) and checks timed out (suspect a sola test degenerates with long fades). 96 confirmed again.

asi.hypothesis: longer fades reduce per-splice flux
asi.rollback_reason: 95.03 < 95.08; more fade time = more dual-pitch overlap
asi.learning: XFADE tested 48/64/96/128 across metrics: 96 optimal. transient_f1 asymptote ~0.91 is aggregate splice-flux noise (attacks verified present with equal contrast); reducing splice count/damage at |T-1|>10% is the only remaining F1 lever and all cheap knobs are exhausted
asi.next_action_hint: consider architectural: dual-window SOLA (long fades in steady content, short near attacks), or accept F1 and work the pitch score (0.43c → <0.2c) or identity (0.9909)

description: Adaptive fade (48 frames when either region hot ≥1.5x avg): 95.04 < 95.08. Short fades near hits splatter more than they localize.

asi.hypothesis: shorter fades near energetic regions localize splice damage
asi.learning: fade-length adaptation in either direction fails; the fade itself is not the damage — the JUMP (phase discontinuity across all non-matched frequencies) is
asi.next_action_hint: pitch lever: chase p95 0.43c→0.2c? or investigate ride pitch wobble sources; or call SOLA done and examine the varispeed/crossover for identity gains

description: FINE_SEARCH_STEPS 4→8: pitch unchanged (0.43c), F1 slightly worse (chaos). Sub-sample refinement already converged; parabolic vertex does the work.

asi.hypothesis: finer fractional splice grid reduces residual pitch wobble
asi.rollback_reason: pitch identical, quality 95.04<95.08 via F1 chaos
asi.learning: p95=0.43c is not limited by splice sub-sample error; it is the fades themselves + estimation windows straddling them. Pitch polish exhausted at this architecture
asi.next_action_hint: state of play: all micro-levers exhausted; remaining scored losses are architectural (low band by design, splice flux inherent to time-domain correction). Consider widening the benchmark (ride scoring) or declaring plateau

description: Correlation-adaptive fade power normalization: 95.05 vs 95.08 — no win. Splice correlations are evidently high enough that the −3 dB dip rarely occurs.

asi.hypothesis: unity-power fade normalization removes mid-fade level dips on low-corr splices
asi.rollback_reason: −0.02 vs best; correlation-matched search keeps ρ high so the dip is rare; residual delta is splice-timing chaos
asi.learning: fade LAW is not the bottleneck either. SOLA is at its architectural quality ceiling on every axis measured
asi.next_action_hint: declare SOLA plateau; final options: benchmark ride scoring, or verify plateau and write summary

description: STREAM_SINC_CUTOFF_SCALE 0.85→0.90: within a hair of best (95.078 vs 95.077), no measurable spec gain. Keep original design value (safer stopband).

asi.hypothesis: less conservative AA cutoff keeps top octave at speedups
asi.rollback_reason: identical metric (+0.001 = tie); mean-spectrum sim insensitive to >16kHz on this material; original 0.85 has safer stopband — simpler/safer wins on a tie
asi.learning: varispeed AA is not a scored bottleneck

description: Preemptive pre-attack splicing (detect at write head, splice while attack is still 13ms from playing): 94.91 < 95.08. F1 0.9084→0.9028.

asi.hypothesis: clear drift right before each attack arrives so no splice is owed near it
asi.rollback_reason: 94.91 < 95.08; extra splices (one per detected attack, ~2/s) cost more than their placement saves — same lesson as quiet-drift-64: minimize splice COUNT
asi.learning: every scheme that ADDS splices loses; every scheme that DELAYS splices loses; only the quiet-gap scheme (which RELOCATES with no count change) won. SOLA verdict final
asi.next_action_hint: SOLA is done. Widen benchmark (ride scoring / third track) or examine non-SOLA stages for real bugs

description: Splice overshoot +96 (fewer, bigger jumps): 94.98 < 95.08. Pitch improved (0.36c p95!) but F1 0.9084→0.9005 — per-splice damage grows superlinearly with jump size.

asi.hypothesis: overshoot jumps trade fewer splices for bigger ones
asi.rollback_reason: 94.98 < 95.08; F1 loss from bigger jumps exceeds cadence gain (jump-size damage superlinear); interesting: pitch p95 improved 0.43→0.36 from fewer fades
asi.learning: splice size/count tradeoff curve fully mapped: 192-frame jumps at natural cadence is the optimum. SOLA definitively closed
asi.next_action_hint: benchmark widening or non-SOLA exploration

description: KEYLOCK_CROSSOVER_HZ 150→120: quality 95.08→95.13. More band corrected (120-150Hz), spec 0.9587→0.9600, pitch 0.43→0.41c, identity −0.002 (more LR8 group delay). Seam test passes.

asi.hypothesis: lower crossover corrects more of the bass line
asi.result: +0.05 net; spec gain systematic (less pitch-following content), F1 unaffected despite CORR_WINDOW < period at 120Hz band bottom
asi.caveat: fights the corpus-settled 150Hz tuning; owner should listening-check bass at tempo gestures before shipping

description: Crossover 120→100 Hz: worse (94.84). F1 drops 0.9083→0.8991 — splices now chop 100-120Hz periods (441 frames >> CORR_WINDOW). 120 Hz is the sweet spot.

asi.hypothesis: continue crossover trend below 120
asi.rollback_reason: spec kept rising (0.9603) but F1 broke (0.899) — corr window can't align 100-120Hz periods; identity also down (group delay)
asi.learning: crossover optimum ~120Hz given CORR_WINDOW=320; going lower requires longer corr window which broke the seam test earlier. 120 final
asi.next_action_hint: note 1Password gpg signing intermittently fails — verify every keep commit landed

description: Crossover 135 Hz: 95.00 — non-monotone dip between 120 (95.13) and 150 (95.08). 120 confirmed best; curve is noisy at ±0.1 scale but 120's spec gain is systematic.

asi.hypothesis: map crossover response curve
asi.rollback_reason: 135 sits in a dip; F1 chaos dominates ±0.005 while spec trend is smooth (0.9587@150, 0.9595@135, 0.9600@120, 0.9603@100)
asi.learning: spec rises smoothly as crossover falls; F1 collapses below ~110 (corr window). 120 balances
asi.next_action_hint: keep 120; consider CORR_WINDOW+crossover joint move later if seam test can be satisfied

description: Crossover 110 + CORR_WINDOW 384: 94.81 (worse) and pitch-drift regression test fails (220Hz→216.5Hz at ratio 1.25). Longer corr window biases landings into real pitch error. Direction closed.

asi.hypothesis: longer corr window unlocks lower crossover
asi.rollback_reason: quality worse AND real pitch drift (27 cents flat at ratio 1.25 on a 220Hz sine — the corr window biases splices onto the wrong period grid)
asi.learning: CORR_WINDOW is hard-constrained by pitch accuracy, not just the seam test; crossover 120 + CORR 320 is the final operating point
asi.next_action_hint: crossover/SOLA fully closed; whole engine parameter space exhausted. Widen benchmark or finalize

description: One-pole rate smoothing before varispeed: breaks sample-exact timestamped retargets (contract tests) and pitch didn't improve (0.42c) — staircase is NOT the wobble source. Discarded.

asi.hypothesis: C1-continuous embedded rate improves keylock slope-tracking during rides
asi.rollback_reason: engine_latency retarget contract tests fail (smoothing delays the exact landing); pitch unchanged — delay-matched inversion already cancels the staircase exactly
asi.learning: residual 0.41c wobble is from splice fades (confirmed by overshoot exp: fewer fades → 0.36c). Ride pitch is at its architectural floor
asi.next_action_hint: add 3rd track, re-validate the two kept wins for generality

description: Harness: add 3rd scored track (Cold Heart, pop-dance 116bpm). New effective baseline 95.50 on the 3-track metric. Track B remains the weakest (F1 0.836-0.892).

asi.hypothesis: 3rd track broadens material coverage before final validation
asi.finding: C (Cold Heart) scores between A and B; B (Hot Stuff) still worst on F1. Note: A's per-rate F1 shifted vs 2-track runs — crossover-120 splice chaos, same avg
asi.next: re-validate crossover 150→120 keep on the 3-track metric (it contradicts corpus-settled tuning; must not be 2-track overfit)

description: Re-validate crossover on 3-track metric: 150 Hz scores 95.34 vs 120 Hz's 95.50. The 150→120 change generalizes across all three tracks (spec +0.0022, F1 +0.003, pitch better). 120 confirmed.

asi.hypothesis: check crossover-120 keep wasn't 2-track overfit
asi.rollback_reason: 150 is worse on the 3-track metric too; revert restores 120
asi.finding: crossover 120 win is general: spec gain systematic on every track, F1 neutral-positive, pitch 0.41 vs 0.43. Remaining caveat is purely perceptual (owner listening check on 120-150Hz bass under splices)
asi.next_action_hint: re-validate quiet-gap splicing ablation on 3-track metric, then update prompt and continue exploring

description: Ablation on 3-track metric: quiet-gap splicing disabled → 95.17 vs 95.50 (F1 0.9162→0.9052). Both kept DSP wins now validated on 3 tracks. Restored.

asi.hypothesis: validate quiet-gap win generality via ablation on 3 tracks
asi.rollback_reason: ablation worse by −0.34 (F1 −0.011 across tracks) — quiet-gap win is general; revert restores it
asi.finding: final validated state: quiet-gap splicing (+0.34) + crossover 120 (+0.17) over the original engine on the 3-track metric
asi.next_action_hint: update prompt.md summary; then explore remaining: per-track B weakness (disco high-band density) or accept plateau and keep monitoring

description: Landing-energy penalty (0.02×relative RMS) in splice candidate scoring: 95.49 vs 95.50 — statistical tie, slightly negative. Correlation term already implicitly avoids bad landings.

asi.hypothesis: bias all splice landings toward quieter audio via per-candidate energy penalty
asi.rollback_reason: tie/−0.01 — no benefit, added complexity; normalized correlation is scale-blind but the quiet-gap trigger already captures the placement gain
asi.learning: candidate scoring is saturated; correlation + small distance penalty is the right objective
asi.next_action_hint: few untried levers remain; consider testing stereo width preservation or accept steady state

description: SEARCH_RANGE 160→128: 95.39 < 95.50 (F1 −0.003). 160 confirmed optimal from both directions on the 3-track metric.

asi.hypothesis: smaller search range converges drift tighter with less period-grid wandering
asi.rollback_reason: worse — narrower search misses better-correlated landings
asi.learning: SEARCH_RANGE 160 optimal bidirectionally. Full SOLA parameter space now mapped on the 3-track metric
asi.next_action_hint: steady state reached at 95.50; write session summary, then continue low-intensity exploration or await user direction

description: HARD_TRIGGER 320→384 (alone): bit-identical output (95.502, every secondary identical) — the hard-force path never fires on these renders; postpones always resolve below 320. Revert to original constant.

asi.hypothesis: more runway before forced splices lets postpones find better spots
asi.rollback_reason: no-op: identical output proves HARD forcing never triggers on real music at DJ rates — splice damage all comes from the regular DRIFT/quiet-gap path
asi.learning: also confirmed this iteration: side-channel quality good (spec 0.95-0.98, image preserved by lockstep splices), output bit-invariant across callback sizes 64-1024. Engine is robust; scored space saturated at 95.50
asi.next_action_hint: remaining value is perceptual validation (render crossover-120 listening pairs) or new benchmark dimensions; no DSP knob left with an untested direction

description: Graded quiet gate: required landing quietness relaxes 0.6×→1.2× avg as drift grows 96→192, so splices fire at the quietest available moment in their window. 95.50→95.58; F1 +0.006 on all 3 tracks (A/B/C each up).

asi.hypothesis: graded gate = splice at the quietest moment available, never delayed past the trigger
asi.result: +0.08 quality; F1 gain general (all tracks); pitch 0.41→0.46c (more splices, sub-JND); rt 78→65x from extra region_rms calls (still 65x realtime)
asi.why_it_worked: combines the two failed extremes correctly: strict gate at low drift (avoids extra splices) + lenient near trigger (never postpones); unlike fixed 0.75 gate which loosened everywhere
asi.next: tune the lenient endpoint (1.2): try 1.0 and 1.5; consider caching region_rms to recover throughput

description: Graded gate endpoint 1.2→1.5: worse (95.08, F1 −0.007, pitch 0.46→0.60c — too many splices in loud audio) and checks timed out. 1.2 endpoint stands.

asi.hypothesis: even more lenient endpoint near trigger
asi.rollback_reason: 95.08 < 95.58; gate 1.5 admits loud landings early → more, worse splices; also 2nd checks timeout observed under heavy-splice configs (long-running sola/keylock tests?)
asi.learning: endpoint 1.2 is on the good side; try 1.0 next to bracket from below
asi.next_action_hint: test endpoint 1.0

description: Graded gate endpoint 1.2→1.0: worse (95.50 vs 95.58, F1 0.9223→0.9169). Endpoint bracketed: 1.0 too strict, 1.5 too loose, 1.2 optimal.

asi.hypothesis: bracket graded-gate endpoint from below
asi.rollback_reason: 1.0 endpoint misses useful near-trigger placements; 1.2 confirmed optimal (bracketed both sides)
asi.learning: graded quiet gate final: 0.6→1.2 over drift 96→192. Session best now 95.58
asi.next_action_hint: update prompt.md; consider recovering throughput (region_rms called 2x/block during pending drift — could cache) as a perf-neutral cleanup, or continue exploration

description: Graded-gate window 320→160: worse (95.49 vs 95.58, F1 0.9223→0.9190). The wide window's blur is a feature — it keeps the whole landing neighborhood (search ±160) quiet, not just the fade spot.

asi.hypothesis: shorter gate window resolves inter-hit gaps more precisely
asi.rollback_reason: 95.49 < 95.58; the 320 window usefully requires the whole candidate neighborhood quiet (search range ±160 means the actual landing can be far from the checked spot — a wide window covers that spread)
asi.learning: gate window = CORR_WINDOW is right for the same reason the correlation window is 320: candidates spread across ±SEARCH_RANGE
asi.next_action_hint: graded gate fully tuned. Next: maybe apply graded logic to the outgoing-vs-incoming asymmetry (outgoing span always plays — only landing needs the gate?)

description: Landing-only graded gate (drop outgoing-span check): 95.50 vs 95.58. The outgoing check matters — fading out mid-hit smears the hit even though it 'plays anyway'.

asi.hypothesis: only the landing needs to be quiet; outgoing plays regardless
asi.rollback_reason: 95.50 < 95.58; wrong — fading OUT of loud audio replaces its tail with different content, exactly as audible as a bad landing
asi.learning: symmetric gate confirmed; graded quiet gate is final as kept in #43
asi.next_action_hint: gate variants exhausted; next frontier would be splice-free correction (architectural) or more corpus breadth

description: Locally-quiet cap on graded gate (min with 0.9× fast local RMS): pitch fully recovered to 0.41/0.51c as predicted, but F1 0.9223→0.9127 — the cap also blocks the productive 1.0-1.2× gate tail on music. Net 95.39 < 95.58.

asi.hypothesis: quiet must mean locally quiet; uniform content gets no early splices
asi.rollback_reason: diagnosis was right (sine pitch recovered exactly) but any cap tight enough to block uniform content also clips the 1.0-1.2×avg gate range where a third of the music F1 gain lives (endpoint-1.0 test showed the same −0.005)
